extracted.intended_audience: Associated Press member newspapers, wire editors, and general newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and notices for Associated Press members about transmitting news dispatches subject to British wartime censorship and release stipulations, embedded in a general news report. Emphasizes how to mark, transmit, and respect embargoed material for wire service distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide strictly by British censor release stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: “ALL MEMBERS ARE EARNESTLY REQUESTED TO ABIDE STRICTLY BY THE RELEASES IMPOSED BY THE BRITISH CENSOR AS INDICATED ON SUCH DISPATCHES AS CARRY NOTICE OF THESE RELEASES.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explains that the British censor may withhold news until a fixed release time or require that transmission not start until that time; members are urged to adhere strictly to those stipulations. It notes that strict adherence is earnestly requested to avoid adverse action by authorities and to respect release confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispatches must carry notice of release
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispatches subject to censorship and embargoes should carry explicit notice indicating the release conditions (e.g., 'advance', release time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly refers to 'dispatches as carry notice of these releases' and shows examples like 'SPECIAL NEWS SERVICE ADVANCE FOR PMS OF WEDNESDAY, SEPT. 18.' Use such labels/datelines to indicate embargoed material so recipients know the censor-imposed restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not delay wire transmission until hour of release (trust newspapers to obey releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author opposed a proposal 'that the Associated Press not start sending the copy until hour of release' and argued against postponing transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale given: newspapers have their own interest in abiding by releases (they benefit by getting matter into type). Therefore, continue sending copy under release notice rather than withholding transmission until the exact release hour, to avoid transmission inefficiencies introduced by delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid violating the confidence imposed by AP release restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must not publish or otherwise violate the confidence of material sent under release stipulations, as such violations could provoke adverse action by authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page expresses concern that individual papers might violate confidence imposed upon the Associated Press, which could result in 'some dangerous adverse action by the authorities.' Strict adherence and internal discipline are therefore urged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of transmission delays and attribute causes carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Trans-Atlantic transmission is imperfect, and delays occur for many reasons; the presence of censorship can complicate attribution of delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes that transmission delays have been unusually severe in wartime and that users may be unable to determine causes; censorship was sometimes blamed though delays existed before censorship. Guidance implies editors should be mindful of technical delays and not assume censorship as sole cause.
